To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optic tectal fate is specified by a combination of positive and negative interactions between genes and that the tectum is regionalised along the anteroposterior and dorsoventral axes by the same mechanisms.
the optic tectal fate is induced by a combination of Pax2, En, and Otx2 and that these three genes are in a positive regulatory loop for their expression.
the tectum is specified as a result of the interplay of several signalling molecules such as Fgf8, Shh, Otx2, Gbx2, En1, Pax2, Pax6, Pax5, and Ephrin A2/A5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the optic tectal fate is induced and how the tectum acquires its regional characteristics and polarisation.
the molecular mechanisms of regionalisation and polarisation in the optic tetcum.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that control the regionalisation and polarity in the tectal primordium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mesencephalic alar plate becomes polarised into a rostrocaudal gradient and a dorsoventral gradient by a combination of inductive signals from the metencephalic boundary (organiser), the diencephalic roof plate and the mesencephalonic floor plate, and by repressive interactions between genes that have been expressed in the presumptive dencephalon, the mesencephalion, and the metencephalion.
the tectum is formed as a result of the interactions of a number of signalling molecules and transcription factors.
the optic tectal fate is determined by the combination of the expression patterns of Otx2 and En1/P2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a tectum can be induced from the diencephalic alar plate by misexpression of Pax2 or En, and that a tectal fate can be maintained by positive autoregulatory loops of Pax2/5 and En1/2, and by repression of Gbx2.
the brain vesicles are not the primary determinants of brain regionalisation.
the optic tectal fate is induced by the combination of Pax2/5 and En, and that the posterior limit of the tecta is defined as the boundary of Gbx2 and Otx2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a mosaic of different domains and that these domains are defined by the expression of different genes.

the brain vesicles that are defined by expression of Otx and Gbx genes may be the primary units of regionalisation and that the brain vesicular boundaries work as organisers for the regionalisation and differentiation of the brain.
the tectum is a highly regionalised organ and that the regionalisation is achieved by interactions among the genes Pax2, Otx2, En, Fgf8, and Gbx2.
